title: Semester and Yearbook
premise: Bram Hartwell, a nonbinary debate champion at Crestline Academy, has perfected the art of being fine — until their best friend Juniper vanishes overnight, leaving behind a set of keys to the school's abandoned yearbook room. Following the keys, Bram uncovers a hidden archive Juniper kept: proof that Crestline's founding family quietly erased students like them from every yearbook, and that Juniper was close to exposing it. As Bram races the state championship circuit and a final audition for a scholarship they no longer want on its old terms, they assemble an unlikely found family of rivals, outcasts, and one very stubborn teacher. In the climax, Bram wins the championship nobody thought mattered, then forfeits the scholarship audition to read the erased names aloud at graduation. The book ends with the school printing a corrected yearbook — and Bram finally signing their own name in full.
about_author: Isandro Nakamura is a former high-school debater who spent three years coaching forensics in coastal Oregon before turning to fiction full-time. They write stories about kids who inherit more than they were promised.

chapters.title: The Art of Being Fine
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. We meet Bram mid-debate, winning rounds effortlessly while losing every argument at home with their father about college, name, and future. Establishes the 'fine' mask and the friendship with Juniper as the one place it slips. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as competence.

chapters.title: Keys
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Juniper misses their traditional Friday diner ritual, then misses school, then stops answering entirely. Police call it a runaway; Bram knows better. At Juniper's locker sits an envelope of keys labeled only 'you'll know.' Emotional beat: dread cracking the mask open.

chapters.title: Room 114
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The keys open the sealed yearbook room, where Bram finds Juniper's secret archive: decades of photos with certain students cut out or never printed. First clue points to the Whitlock founding family. Emotional beat: awe curdling into anger.

chapters.title: Objection, Relevance
chapters.summary: Rival debater Theo Okafor's POV. Theo notices Bram distracted at the regional qualifier and covers for them without knowing why. A grudging alliance forms over shared suspicion of Headmaster Whitlock. Emotional beat: rivalry softening into reluctant respect.

chapters.title: What the Archive Keeps
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Digging deeper, Bram finds a 1978 student — 'S. Marlowe' — whose records vanish after a protest. Juniper's notes connect Marlowe to the current scholarship endowment. Emotional beat: inheritance revealed as something stolen, not given.

chapters.title: Home Court Disadvantage
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram's father announces he's arranged a meeting with Whitlock about the scholarship, forcing Bram to perform gratitude while hiding the investigation. A fight ends with Bram walking out. Emotional beat: the cost of staying invisible at home.

chapters.title: The Librarian Who Remembers
chapters.summary: Ms. Ferreira's POV. The school librarian, a Crestline alum, recognizes what Bram is searching for and admits she knew S. Marlowe — her cousin. She gives Bram Marlowe's last letter but warns that Whitlock watches the archive. Emotional beat: grief passed down like a relay baton.

chapters.title: Semifinals, Interrupted
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. At semifinals, Bram freezes when they spot Whitlock photographing attendees — including someone who looks like Juniper in the crowd. Theo throws their own round to buy Bram time to chase the lead. Emotional beat: sacrifice without explanation.

chapters.title: A Sighting, Not a Sign
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The trail leads to a bus depot and a dead end — or a deliberate misdirection. Bram realizes Juniper left the keys as a map, not a cry for help, and starts reading the archive as instructions rather than evidence. Emotional beat: hope restructured as method.

chapters.title: Found Family, Assembled
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram convenes an unlikely crew: Theo, Ms. Ferreira, yearbook dropout Priya, and quiet custodian Mr. Ansel, who has keys to everything. They divide the archive work. Emotional beat: the first true feeling of belonging, chosen rather than assigned.

chapters.title: The Endowment Papers
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya decodes financial pages showing the Whitlock scholarship is funded by assets seized from Marlowe's family after the protest. The 'generous inheritance' is a laundering of theft. Emotional beat: righteous fury with nowhere safe to put it.

chapters.title: Whitlock Invites Bram to Tea
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Whitlock, aware of the archive visits, offers Bram the scholarship early — contingent on signing a confidentiality agreement. Bram stalls, saying yes to everything and nothing. Emotional beat: the mask weaponized.

chapters.title: Juniper's Voice Mail
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. A delayed voice mail arrives: Juniper is safe, hiding with Marlowe's surviving sister, waiting for proof before coming back. They ask Bram to finish what they started. Emotional beat: relief braided with the weight of being trusted.

chapters.title: State Championship Bracket
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The team advances to states; Theo and Bram must now partner instead of compete. Late-night practice becomes confession — Theo reveals why they debate: a brother expelled from Crestline under Whitlock's father. Emotional beat: two masks lowered at once.

chapters.title: Break-In, Breakthrough
chapters.summary: Mr. Ansel's POV. Using his master keys, Ansel helps the crew copy the original board minutes proving the erasure was policy, not accident. They're nearly caught by security; Ferreira takes the blame to protect the students. Emotional beat: adults choosing kids over institutions.

chapters.title: The Round That Matters
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. State championship final: the resolution is ironically about institutional accountability. Bram debates with everything the archive taught them and wins. Emotional beat: triumph that feels like rehearsal for something larger.

chapters.title: Terms and Conditions
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Whitlock congratulates Bram privately and makes the threat explicit: sign, or the scholarship — and Juniper's readmission — disappear. Bram asks for one night to decide. Emotional beat: fear met with stillness.

chapters.title: Final Audition
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The scholarship audition requires a speech about legacy. Instead of the prepared remarks, Bram reads the erased names from the archive, ending with S. Marlowe and Juniper, and declines the tainted award on record. Emotional beat: the argument at home, finally won by losing gracefully.

chapters.title: Fallout
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The speech leaks. Students walk out; alumni demand answers; Bram's father arrives furious — then, seeing the crowd holding printed names, goes quiet and stands beside his child. Emotional beat: reconciliation without apology demanded.

chapters.title: Marlowe Returns
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Juniper comes back with Marlowe's sister, now elderly, who addresses the assembled school. The board, cornered by press and the copied minutes, suspends Whitlock pending investigation. Emotional beat: justice arriving imperfectly but undeniably.

chapters.title: Proofs and Corrections
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The crew spends graduation week rebuilding the yearbook with the restored names, photos reprinted from negatives Ansel kept hidden for forty years. Bram writes the foreword. Emotional beat: repair as collective craft.

chapters.title: Signed, In Full
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. At graduation, the corrected yearbooks are handed out and Bram signs Juniper's copy with their full chosen name for the first time. Father watching, friends surrounding, future unwritten but theirs. Emotional beat: identity claimed, inheritance reclaimed, family found.
